Observation: - Dirty Pretty Things: Dirty Pretty Things were an English rock band fronted by Carl Barât, a member of The Libertines. The band formed in June 2005 after Barât's previous band The Libertines went on hiatus. The lineup consisted of Barât on vocals and guitar, Didz Hammond on bass guitar, Anthony Rossomando on guitar and Gary Powell on drums. They released their debut album Waterloo to Anywhere on 8 May 2006, which peaked at #3 in the UK album charts.
- The Libertines: The Libertines are an English rock band, formed in London in 1997 by frontmen Carl Barât (vocals/guitar) and Pete Doherty (vocals/guitar). The band, centred on the songwriting partnership of Barât and Doherty, also included John Hassall (bass guitar) and Gary Powell (drums) for most of its recording career. The band became a prominent garage rock revival act in the early 2000s and gained an ardent cult following. They broke through with their debut album Up the Bracket, released in 2002 to critical acclaim and commercial success.
- Carl Barât: Carl Ashley Raphael Barât (born 6 June 1978) is an English musician and actor, best known for being the co-frontman of the Libertines. He was also the frontman and lead guitarist of Dirty Pretty Things, and has released two solo albums.
